## Length of a segment

### Problem
A circle is inscribed in an equilateral triangle $ABC$ as shown at the right. The segment $DE$ is tangent to the circle, perpendicular to $AB$, and its endpoints $D$ and $E$ lie on $BC$ and $AB$, respectively. If the radius of the circle is 1, find the length $|BE|$ and express it as simply as you can with rational denominator.

![Figure for Jerry Heuer heuer-2010-p04](study/assets/asset-heuer-2010-p04-heuer-2010-p04.png)

### Solution (adapted from the official solution)
The length $|BE| = \sqrt{3} - 1$.

![Figure for Jerry Heuer heuer-2010-p04-solution](study/assets/asset-heuer-2010-p04-solution-heuer-2010-p04-solution.png)

Each side of the equilateral triangle has length $2\sqrt{3}$. Let $O$ be the center of the circle, $F$ the point of tangency of side $AB$, and $K$ the point of tangency on line $DE$.

Then $OKEF$ is a square of side 1, so $|BE| = |BF| - 1 = \sqrt{3} - 1$.

### Conceptual Explanation
In an equilateral triangle with inradius $r=1$, the half-side $|BF| = \frac{r}{\tan 30^\circ} = \sqrt{3}$. Because $DE \perp AB$ and $DE$ is tangent to the in-circle, the radii to the points of tangency $F$ on $AB$ and $K$ on $DE$ form a square $OKEF$ of side length 1, making $|FE|=1$. Thus $|BE| = |BF| - |FE| = \sqrt{3} - 1$.

### Key Technique
Tangency points and perpendicular tangents to a circle create squares with the center; inradius relations in equilateral triangles.
